verdict.rationale: React's docs say it can stream HTML while data is still being fetched, progressively filling in the remaining content, and that frameworks implementing its architecture can fetch data in async server components. That points to a first-party data-loading and progressive loading UI capability, but the pack never names Suspense, a resource-style primitive, or reactive data state. missing for 10: explicit Suspense boundary/fallback documentation, a resource or data primitive that treats server data as reactive state, client-side loading-state handling, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can treat server-loaded data as reactive state and build a responsive loading UI for it using resource and suspense primitives

citations.quote: On the server, React lets you start streaming HTML while you’re still fetching data, progressively filling in the remaining content before any JavaScript code loads.
Frameworks that implement it let you fetch data in asynchronous components that run on the server or even during the build.
